name: AudioToStructuredData

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: 2-pass enhancement adds ~60s for typical 5-min recording
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium -- two LLM calls per document

known_limitations: Requires audio/video input; cannot process text-only input without bypassing Transcriber
TranscriptEnhancer is tuned for Finnish; other languages require prompt customisation

Drives Transcriber on the hosted path, so the transcript it extracts from carries no timestamps and no speaker labels. Use cases needing time-coded citations, subtitles, or speaker attribution must not use this module -- decompose into an explicit transcription step (Transcriber with whisper_local for speakers, ParallelTranscriber with response_format='srt' for timestamps only) + SchemaGenerator + DataExtractor.

name: DocumentsToStructuredData

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Vision parser adds latency but handles complex layouts better
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium -- LLM extraction call per document

known_limitations: Complex scanned documents or accuracy-critical complex layouts should use VisionExtractor instead
Multi-page extraction may lose cross-page context

name: RAGWorkflow

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Larger top_k improves recall but increases generation cost
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium -- embedding + generation calls

known_limitations: Requires PostgreSQL with pgvector extension
Initial indexing required before querying

name: Transcriber

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: gpt-4o-transcribe is more accurate but slower than whisper
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- single transcription call

known_limitations: Does not produce structured output -- use Extractor downstream

Built-in transcript enhancement (enhanced_transcript=True) is Finnish-tuned; calls TranscriptEnhancer internally. For audio input, set this option instead of adding a separate TranscriptEnhancer step. For non-Finnish audio, enhancement needs prompt customisation -- default off and flag it.

The hosted models (whisper, whisper-1, gpt-4o-transcribe) return plain text only: .segments, .srt_content and .vtt_content stay None, and diarization/speaker_count/min_speakers/max_speakers are silently ignored. Timestamps and speaker labels require transcription_model='whisper_local'.
whisper_local requires a self-hosted transcription endpoint (local_api_base + local_api_key); transcribe() raises ValueError without both. Confirm the user has one before selecting this path.
Speaker labels are exposed on .segments only. .srt_content and .vtt_content are built by segments_to_srt/segments_to_vtt, which read start/end/text and drop every other key.

name: TranscriptEnhancer

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Adds ~60s per 5-min recording; significantly reduces ASR errors
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low-medium -- two LLM passes

known_limitations: Tuned for Finnish; other languages require prompt customisation
Should not be used when transcript faithfulness is more important than correctness

name: Extractor

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Structured output via schema improves precision at cost of one schema-generation call
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium -- schema generation + extraction calls

known_limitations: Requires schema or field requirements to extract against

When provider=azure_openai: bare dict and list[dict] Pydantic field types cause a 400 error â€” Azure OpenAI structured output requires additionalProperties:false on every object. Replace with named sub-models using ConfigDict(extra='forbid'). E.g. define class Medication(BaseModel) with model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid') and use list[Medication] instead of list[dict].

ExtractionRequirements field_type enum does not include plain 'dict'. For nested objects use field_type 'str' in requirements JSON; for arrays of objects use 'list[dict]'. Never write field_type: 'dict' directly.

name: VisionExtractor

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: High reasoning_effort significantly improves complex layout handling
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: high -- vision calls ~10x local parsing cost

known_limitations: Max ~20MB per file
Not suitable for audio input
Could be more expensive for large document batches -- prefer DocumentsToStructuredData for plain text PDFs

name: DocumentClassifier

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Zero-shot with good category descriptions is usually sufficient
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- single classification call

known_limitations: Categories must be clearly defined; ambiguous categories reduce accuracy
Does not produce structured field extraction -- combine with Extractor for full pipeline

name: PgVectorStore

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Larger top_k improves recall at cost of generation context
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- embedding calls only

known_limitations: Requires PostgreSQL with pgvector extension (`pip install gaik[pg-vector-store]`)
Database must be set up separately before use

name: LLMJudge

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Panel of judges (LLMJudgePanel) increases reliability at higher cost
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium -- one or more LLM judgement calls

known_limitations: LLM judges can be inconsistent; use LLMJudgePanel for critical decisions
Not a substitute for human review in safety-critical workflows

name: ParallelTranscriber

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Parallel FFmpeg chunking transcribes long media far faster than the sequential Transcriber; gpt-4o-transcribe is more accurate but slower than whisper
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- one transcription call per chunk

known_limitations: Requires FFmpeg + ffprobe on PATH (system dependency); no pure-Python fallback
Does not produce structured output -- use Extractor downstream
Overlap deduplication is SRT-based; use response_format='srt' for the cleanest chunk merging

Produces timestamps but never speaker labels, on any backend. gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize requests diarized output and parses the speaker field, then discards it when building the SRT (and TranscriptionResult exposes only .content, so it cannot be recovered); the whisper_local backend hardcodes diarization=False in its request payload. For speaker attribution use Transcriber(transcription_model='whisper_local', diarization=True).

The whisper_local backend takes its endpoint from api_config['api_base'] (required) and api_config['key'] or ['api_key'] (optional -- the auth header is omitted when empty). This differs from Transcriber, which uses the local_api_base/local_api_key constructor kwargs and requires both.

name: MultiSourceReportGenerator

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Single-call mode: one LLM call writes the whole report â€” fast and cheap, higher hallucination risk. Agentic mode (agentic=True): each section is drafted independently and fact-checked by a diff-editor reviewer â€” higher accuracy, more API calls (N draft + N reviewer per section). Vision/multimodal parsers add latency but handle complex layouts.
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: high -- scales with number of source files and number of report sections; agentic mode multiplies LLM calls by section count

known_limitations: Orchestrates existing GAIK parsers/transcriber/extractor; no new parsing logic -- inherits each sub-component's limits
Long-form synthesis cost grows with sources x sections; agentic mode is significantly more expensive than single-call
Report content is drawn only from supplied evidence; it does not browse or fetch external sources
Agentic mode requires the multi-source-report-generator-agentic extra (langgraph); DOCX export requires multi-source-report-generator-docx extra and Pandoc system binary

name: LLMJudgePanel

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Panel of 2+ judges with majority vote reduces single-model bias at higher latency and cost
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: high -- one LLM call per judge per item

known_limitations: Requires at least 2 LLMJudge instances; diverse providers give strongest debiasing
Not a substitute for human review in safety-critical workflows

name: ExtractionEvaluator

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Semantic mode uses LLMJudge for free-text fields; adds LLM cost but tolerates paraphrasing
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low (exact) to medium (semantic)

known_limitations: match_mode='semantic' requires a judge instance
Does not handle nested/list field comparison -- flatten before evaluating

name: RAGEvaluator

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: 4 LLM calls per item (faithfulness, relevance, precision, recall); context_recall only when ground_truth provided
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium-high -- 3-4 judge calls per RAG item

known_limitations: context_recall requires ground_truth; skipped otherwise (skip_context_recall=True by default)
Scores are Likert 1-5 normalized to 0-1; not calibrated against human raters

name: BatchEvaluationRunner

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Sequential execution; on_error='skip' continues past failures at risk of incomplete results
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: determined by the pipeline callable

known_limitations: Sequential only; no parallel execution
on_error='raise' stops on first failure; 'skip' records failures in result.failures

name: SchemaGenerator

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Two LLM calls (structure detection + field parsing); flat schemas need only one pass
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- two small structured-output calls per schema generation

known_limitations: Supports Azure OpenAI and OpenAI only; no Anthropic/Google for structured output
field_type enum is limited: str/int/float/bool/list[str]/date/decimal/list[dict] -- 'dict' is not valid
Azure OpenAI structured output rejects bare dict/list[dict] field types -- replace with named Pydantic sub-models

name: TextToSpeech

quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- single TTS API call per synthesize() call

known_limitations: Supports only 'fi' (Finnish) and 'en' (English) language options
Voice names are provider-specific; default 'marin' is Finnish-optimised

name: PostgresAgent

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Agentic retry loop (max_retries) improves SQL accuracy at cost of latency
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low-medium -- one to three LLM calls per question

known_limitations: Read-only SELECT queries only; no writes, DDL, or data import
Full schema placed in LLM prompt; very large databases need table_allowlist
Requires a live PostgreSQL connection at runtime

name: TabularAgent

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Column profiling is free (plain SQL) and is the main accuracy lever. layout_inference='auto' spends one extra LLM call only on messy sheets
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low-medium -- one to three LLM calls per question, plus one per messy sheet at load

known_limitations: Read-only SELECT queries only; source files are never modified
No charts, regression, or forecasting -- SQL only, no Python execution
Whole profiled schema goes in the LLM prompt; best for small/medium files
In a messy sheet, a data row missing a descriptive field can be dropped as a subtotal

name: FormUnderstander

quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- single structured LLM call per batch of fields

known_limitations: No README available -- sourced from module docstring and source inspection
No example script available
LLM-based labelling; ambiguous field IDs may need parent HTML snippet for context
No extra pip install needed; bundled with base gaik install

name: VisionParser

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: One vision call per page -- slower and costlier than local parsers, but preserves layout, tables, and page boundaries
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium-high -- scales linearly with page count

known_limitations: One vision-model call per page -- cost and latency scale linearly with page count
Requires OpenAI or Azure OpenAI access; there is no local-only mode
convert_image (image input) returns a single markdown string, not a page list -- page provenance applies to PDF input only

name: MultimodalParser

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Slowest parser -- highest accuracy for layout preservation and irregular tables that span pages
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: high -- one premium multimodal call over the whole document

known_limitations: Parses the whole PDF in a single model call and returns flat markdown (ParseResult.clean_markdown) -- page boundaries are NOT preserved, so it cannot support 'file_name|page_number' citations. Use VisionParser when page provenance is required.
PDF input only -- use DocxParser for Word documents
Requires a premium multimodal model from OpenAI/Azure, Anthropic, or Google (pip install gaik[multimodal-parser])

name: DoclingParser

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: OCR and formula enrichment raise accuracy on scanned and scientific documents at a large latency cost on CPU
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: none -- runs locally, no API calls; cost is compute time

known_limitations: Slow without a CUDA-enabled GPU -- OCR and formula enrichment dominate runtime on CPU
ocr_engine choice affects language support and system dependencies ('tesseract_cli' requires a system Tesseract install)
parse_document flattens the document into one text_content string -- no page-level provenance

name: VisionPlusParser

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Docling layout analysis plus a vision model per detected image -- the most accurate option for documents whose figures carry meaning, and the slowest
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium -- one vision call per detected image, not per page

known_limitations: Runs Docling locally AND calls a vision model -- combines both cost profiles
Requires the 'parser' extra plus OpenAI/Azure access
Returns one flat parsed_markdown string -- no page-level provenance

name: DoclingApiClientParser

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Same Docling quality as the local parser but GPU-accelerated server-side -- far faster than local CPU Docling
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: none in API terms; requires service access

known_limitations: Requires access to the Haaga-Helia hosted Docling service. api_base and password are constructor kwargs with NO environment fallback in gaik -- read them from DOCLING_API_BASE / DOCLING_API_PASSWORD in generated code (the convention used by toolkit_demo_app and the OpenShift deployment).
Raises ValueError at construction when either credential is empty
Sends the document to an external service -- unsuitable when data must not leave the local environment
Returns parsed_markdown (not text_content like the local DoclingParser) and flattens pages -- no page-level provenance
Declared under the 'parser' extra because that is where requests is pinned; the client itself does not need docling installed locally

name: PyMuPDFParser

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Fastest parser by a wide margin; accuracy drops on anything but simple text layouts
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: none -- fully local, no API calls

known_limitations: No OCR -- cannot read scanned or image-only PDFs (use DoclingParser)
Simple layouts only; tables and multi-column text degrade badly

Default (use_markdown=True) concatenates pages into one text_content string with no page marker -- no page-level provenance. use_markdown=False inserts '=== PAGE N ===' markers (plus per-line [x:,y:] bounding-box tags) and IS a valid, free/local way to get file_name|page_number citations for text-layer PDFs -- see the reference card's call_page_citations pattern.

name: DocxParser

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Fast and lossless for text and tables; carries no layout or visual information
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: none -- fully local, no API calls

known_limitations: Word documents -- use a PDF parser for PDFs. Declares .doc support (is_supported_file() accepts it), but python-docx's Document() cannot open the legacy binary .doc format -- a real .doc file raises PackageNotFoundError at parse time. Treat only .docx as actually supported.
DOCX has no fixed page model, so page-level citations are not possible
use_markdown=False emits paragraph-index and style markers rather than clean prose

name: Embedder

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Larger embedding models improve retrieval quality at higher cost per chunk
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- embedding calls are cheap relative to generation

known_limitations: RAGWorkflow already performs embedding -- select this directly only when building a custom pipeline that needs to skip or reorder steps
Requires OpenAI or Azure OpenAI access
Accepts LangChain Documents or plain strings; metadata is preserved only for Documents

name: Retriever

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: hybrid_search and re_rank raise recall and precision at the cost of extra computation per query
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: low -- one embedding call per query

known_limitations: Requires an already-constructed Embedder and vector store -- not usable standalone
RAGWorkflow already performs retrieval -- select this directly only for custom pipelines
re_rank downloads a cross-encoder model on first use

name: AnswerGenerator

quality_tradeoffs.speed_vs_accuracy: Larger models give better grounded answers; citations add prompt overhead but make outputs auditable
quality_tradeoffs.cost_sensitivity: medium -- one generation call per query, scaled by context size

known_limitations: RAGWorkflow already performs answer generation -- select this directly only for custom pipelines
Streams by default (stream=True); set stream=False to receive a single string
Citation quality depends entirely on the retrieved context -- it formats citations, it does not verify sources
